actions.action: Isolate the plant away from other houseplants
Check white specks to tell dust from mealybugs (wipe test, look for cottony fluff)
Dab each scale bump and white spot with an alcohol-soaked cotton swab
Alternatively wipe both leaf surfaces with a damp cloth
Spray neem oil or insecticidal soap on leaf undersides and stems, repeating every 5-7 days for 3-4 rounds
Move plant a few feet back from the window or behind a sheer curtain
Gradually move the plant closer to the window over 2-3 weeks
Cut off leaves that are mostly brown or heavily infested
Check that the top 2-3 inches of soil are dry before watering
If drooping continues, unpot the plant and inspect the roots

reason: The answer correctly identifies a sap-sucking pest infestation plus sun stress (calling it scale rather than thrips), and its isolate, alcohol-wipe, neem or insecticidal soap, repeat routine matches what fixed the plant, with nothing harmful.
